arxiv-1906-01268.title: Exploiting Sentential Context for Neural Machine Translation
arxiv-1906-01268.creator: Xing Wang, Zhaopeng Tu, Longyue Wang, Shuming Shi
arxiv-1906-01268.description: Abstract In this work, we present novel approaches to exploit sentential context for neural machine translation (NMT). Specifically, we first show that a shallow sentential context extracted from the top encoder layer only, can improve translation performance via contextualizing the encoding representations of individual words.

arxiv-2110-15175.title: Some remarks on smooth mappings of Hilbert and Banach spaces and their local convexity property
arxiv-2110-15175.creator: Yarema A. Prykarpatskyy 0000-0002-3033-7419, Petro Ya. Pukach 0000-0002-0359-5025, Myroslava I. Vovk 0000-0002-7818-7755, Michal Greguš 0000-0002-8156-8962
arxiv-2110-15175.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Yarema A. Prykarpatskyy 0000-0002-3033-7419, Petro Ya. Pukach 0000-0002-0359-5025, Myroslava I. Vovk 0000-0002-7818-7755, Michal Greguš 0000-0002-8156-8962. We analyze smooth nonlinear mappings for Hilbert and Banach spaces that carry small balls to convex sets, provided that the radius of the balls is small enough.

arxiv-2207-00602.title: Synchronization and random attractors for reaction jump processes
arxiv-2207-00602.creator: Maximilian Engel, Guillermo Olicón-Méndez, Nathalie Unger, Stefanie Winkelmann
arxiv-2207-00602.description: Abstract This work explores a synchronization-like phenomenon induced by common noise for continuous-time Markov jump processes given by chemical reaction networks. A corresponding random dynamical system is formulated in a two-step procedure, at first for the states of the embedded discrete-time Markov chain and then for the augmented Markov chain including also random jump times.

arxiv-2208-06452.title: A Square-Root Kalman Filter Using Only QR Decompositions
arxiv-2208-06452.creator: Kevin S. Tracy
arxiv-2208-06452.description: Abstract The Kalman filter operates by storing a Gaussian description of the state estimate in the form of a mean and covariance. Instead of storing and manipulating the covariance matrix directly, a square-root Kalman filter only forms and updates a triangular matrix square root of the covariance matrix.

arxiv-2208-11966.title: The Artin Component and Simultaneous Resolution via Reconstruction Algebras of Type A A
arxiv-2208-11966.creator: Brian Makonzi
arxiv-2208-11966.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Brian Makonzi. This paper uses noncommutative resolutions of non-Gorenstein singularities to construct classical deformation spaces, by recovering the Artin component of the deformation space of a cyclic surface singularity using only the quiver of the corresponding reconstruction algebra. The relations of the reconstruction algebra are then deformed, and the deformed relations together with variation of the GIT quotient achieve the simultaneous resolution.

arxiv-2401-17945.title: Euclid preparation
arxiv-2401-17945.creator: Euclid Collaboration: A. Kashlinsky, R. G. Arendt, M. L. N. Ashby, F. Atrio-Barandela, R. Scaramella, M. A. Strauss, B. Altieri, A. Amara, S. Andreon, N. Auricchio, M. Baldi, S. Bardelli, R. Bender, C. Bodendorf, E. Branchini, M. Brescia, J. Brinchmann, S. Camera, V. Capobianco, C. Carbone, J. Carre
arxiv-2401-17945.description: Abstract Verifying the fully kinematic nature of the long-known cosmic microwave background (CMB) dipole is of fundamental importance in cosmology. In the standard cosmological model with the Friedman–Lemaitre–Robertson–Walker (FLRW) metric from the inflationary expansion the CMB dipole should be entirely kinematic.

arxiv-2405-06082.title: Thermodynamic Insights into Polyelectrolyte Complexation: A Theoretical Framework
arxiv-2405-06082.creator: Souradeep Ghosh
arxiv-2405-06082.description: Abstract In this study, we propose a theoretical framework to investigate the interactions between flexible polymer chains, specifically polyelectrolytes (PEs). By calculating the system’s free energy while considering position-dependent mutual interactions and chain conformations, we gain insights into the local dielectricity as PEs overlap.

arxiv-2408-08939.title: Oral squamous cell detection using deep learning
arxiv-2408-08939.creator: Samrat Kumar Dev Sharma
arxiv-2408-08939.description: Abstract Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) represents a significant global health concern, with increasing incidence rates and challenges in early diagnosis and treatment planning. Early detection is crucial for improving patient outcomes and survival rates. Despite advances in understanding its molecular mechanisms, late diagnosis remains a substantial challenge in OSCC management.

arxiv-2504-18144.title: The Role of Population III Star Tidal Disruption Events in Black Hole Growth at the Cosmic Dawn
arxiv-2504-18144.creator: Zijian Wang, Yiqiu Ma, Yuxuan Li, Zheng Cai, Chanyan Wang, Qingwen Wu
arxiv-2504-18144.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Zijian Wang, Yiqiu Ma, Yuxuan Li, Zheng Cai, Chanyan Wang, Qingwen Wu. The discovery of supermassive black holes (SMBHs) at high redshifts has intensified efforts to understand their early formation and rapid growth during the cosmic dawn. Using a semi-analytical cosmological framework, we investigate the role of tidal disruption events (TDEs) involving Population III (Pop-III) stars in driving the growth of heavy seed black holes ( 10 4 − 10 6 ​ M ⊙ 10^{4}-10^{6}\,M_{\odot} ).

arxiv-2505-21219.title: Addressing Data Quality Decompensation in Federated Learning via Dynamic Client Selection
arxiv-2505-21219.creator: Qinjun Fei, Nuria Rodríguez-Barroso, María Victoria Luzón, Zhongliang Zhang, Francisco Herrera, [] Department of Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence, Andalusian Research Institute in Data Science and Computational Intelligence (DaSCI), University of Granada, Spain Department of Software Eng
arxiv-2505-21219.description: Abstract In cross-silo Federated Learning (FL), client selection is critical to ensure high model performance, yet it remains challenging due to data quality decompensation, budget constraints, and incentive compatibility. As training progresses, these factors exacerbate client heterogeneity and degrade global performance. Most existing approaches treat these challenges in isolation, making jointly optimizing multiple factors difficult.

arxiv-2506-17891.title: Relation3D: Enhancing Relation Modeling for Point Cloud Instance Segmentation
arxiv-2506-17891.creator: Jiahao Lu, Jiacheng Deng
arxiv-2506-17891.description: Abstract 3D instance segmentation aims to predict a set of object instances in a scene, representing them as binary foreground masks with corresponding semantic labels. Currently, transformer-based methods are gaining increasing attention due to their elegant pipelines and superior predictions. However, these methods primarily focus on modeling the external relationships between scene features and query features through mask attention.

arxiv-2509-13535.title: Crash Report Enhancement with Large Language Models: An Empirical Study DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Conference: ACM International Conference; 978-1-4503-XXXX-X/2018/06 ISBN: ;
arxiv-2509-13535.creator: S M Farah Al Fahim, Md Nakhla Rafi, Zeyang Ma, Dong Jae Kim, Tse-Hsun (Peter) Chen
arxiv-2509-13535.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by S M Farah Al Fahim, Md Nakhla Rafi, Zeyang Ma, Dong Jae Kim, Tse-Hsun (Peter) Chen. Crash reports are central to software maintenance, yet many lack the diagnostic detail developers need to debug efficiently. We examine whether large language models can enhance crash reports by adding fault locations, root-cause explanations, and repair suggestions. We study two enhancement strategies: Direct-LLM , a single-shot approach that uses stack-trace context, and Agentic-LLM , an iterative approach that explores the repository for additional evidence.

arxiv-2602-07817.title: Field conserving adaptive mesh refinement (AMR) scheme on massively parallel adaptive octree meshes
arxiv-2602-07817.creator: Kumar Saurabh, Makrand A. Khanwale, Masado Ishii, Hari Sundar, Baskar Ganapathysubramanian
arxiv-2602-07817.description: Abstract Adaptive mesh refinement (AMR) is widely used to efficiently resolve localized features in time-dependent partial differential equations (PDEs) by selectively refining and coarsening the mesh. However, in long-horizon simulations, repeated intergrid interpolations can introduce systematic drift in conserved quantities, especially for variational discretizations with continuous basis functions.

pmc-10604375.creator: Miguel A Rubio-Herrera, Sara Mera-Carreiro, Andrés Sánchez-Pernaute, Ana M Ramos-Levi, Juan Gambini, Ángel Luis Orteg
pmc-10604375.description: Background: Weight loss before undergoing metabolic and bariatric surgery (MBS) has been suggested to reduce perioperative complications, although with controversial results. pmc-11290069.description: BackgroundDrug resistance, including Adriamycin-based therapeutic resistance, remains a challenge in breast cancer (BC) treatment. Accumulating evidence suggests that tRNA-Derived small RNAs (tDRs) are associated the physiological and pathological processes in multiple cancers.

pmc-12400322.title: Safety and efficacy of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists in individuals with type 2 diabetes mellitus fasting during Ramadan: a systematic review and meta-analysis

pmc-12400322.description: BACKGROUNDData on the use of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) in individuals with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) during Ramadan fasting is limited. No meta-analysis has summarized the safety and effectiveness of GLP-1RAs in these situations.AIMTo evaluate the safety and efficacy of GLP-1RA in patients with T2DM fasting during Ramadan.

pmc-12654444.title: The Change in Healthcare-Associated Infections in Intensive Care Units Associated with the Coronavirus Disease 2019 in Taiwan
pmc-12654444.creator: Chien-Ying Wang, Yu-Hsuan Chen, Chih-Chun Hsiao, Chun-Gu Cheng, Chun-An Cheng, Doina Azoicai
pmc-12654444.description: Background and Objectives: Changes in the incidence of healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) during the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic and during periods with fewer or more COVID-19 cases have been inconclusively studied. Compared with 2015, in 2019, the abundances of the microorganisms Klebsiella pneumoniae and Enterococcus faecium increased in intensive care units (ICUs) in Taiwan.

pmc-12937301.title: Impact of a Volunteer‐Delivered Spiritual Care Strategy on Preventing Post‐Intensive Care Syndrome‐Family in Relatives of Critically Ill ICU Patients: A Quasi‐Experimental Study

pmc-12937301.description: BackgroundFamily members of critically ill patients are at increased risk of developing psychological disorders after ICU discharge, a condition known as Post‐Intensive Care Syndrome‐Family (PICS‐F). pmc-13161707.title: A Rare Case of Bee Sting-Induced Facial Palsy: Diagnosis, Treatment, and Recovery
pmc-13161707.creator: Balasubramaniam Arun, Kandhasamy Sasirekha, Jayakumar Priya, Balasubramanian Ganesan
pmc-13161707.description: IntroductionBee stings commonly cause allergic reactions ranging from mild local symptoms to severe systemic manifestations. Neurological complications are rare, and isolated facial nerve palsy is particularly uncommon.Case presentationThis case report a 25-year-old man who developed right-sided facial paralysis one day after a periauricular bee sting. There were no systemic or central neurological deficits.
